Operations PortalCMS GitHub Actions - Outstanding GitHub-Side Setup
Repository: access-ci-org/Operations_PortalCMS_Django

Status: ci.yml, deploy-beta.yml, and deploy-production.yml define the release
promotion path. The items below are repo/org SETTINGS, not files, so they cannot
be applied by committing code. Each must be configured directly in GitHub
(Settings UI, gh CLI, or the REST/GraphQL API) before a release tag can run a
real beta-to-production deployment.

====================================================================
1) Beta and production environments
====================================================================
- Create a "beta" environment with no required reviewers so a validated release
  tag deploys automatically. Allow tags matching v*.*.* in its deployment
  branch/tag policy, then add the beta ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD as an environment
  secret. Manual migration retries are also dispatched from the exact release tag.
- Create a "production" environment and allow tags matching v*.*.* in its
  deployment branch/tag policy.
- Add required reviewers to production and prevent self-review. This environment
  is the manual approval gate before the deploy-production job starts.
- A production migration retry is dispatched with GitHub CLI from the exact
  immutable release tag, verifies successful beta smoke tests for that tag and
  commit, and then reaches this separate Environment approval.
- Add the production ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD as an environment secret.
- Keep INFRASTRUCTURE_REPO_TOKEN_PORTAL at repository or organization scope.
  Beta and production pre-deployment checks need it before an environment-gated
  deployment job starts; do not put the token in CI jobs.

====================================================================
2) Tag protection ruleset for v*.*.*
====================================================================
- Create a tag ruleset restricting creation/update/deletion of tags matching
  v*.*.* to specific actors/teams.
- Disallow deletion of matching tags.
- Prefer annotated or signed tags for production releases.
- deploy-production.yml already enforces "tag must be reachable from main"
  in its validate-tag job, but that is a workflow-side check, not a
  substitute for the GitHub-side ruleset (a ruleset stops a bad tag from
  being created in the first place).

====================================================================
3) Branch ruleset / protection on main
====================================================================
- Require pull requests before merging to main.
- Require the ci.yml "CI Summary" job as a required status check.
- Require CODEOWNERS review for changes under .github/ (CODEOWNERS file
  already lists @jyssy @jpnavarro @ericblau for this path).
- Dismiss stale approvals on new commits.
- Require conversation resolution before merge.

====================================================================
4) Self-hosted runner labels
====================================================================
- Beta and production pre-deployment/deployment jobs target:
  runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, deployment, portalcms]
- Confirm a self-hosted runner is registered with all four labels
  (especially the app-specific "portalcms" label - this is not shared with
  Operations_ServiceIndex_Django's runner, which uses "serviceindex").
  Without a matching runner, those jobs queue indefinitely and never fail
  loudly.
- ci.yml's code-quality/dependency-review/summary jobs only require the
  generic "self-hosted" label.

====================================================================
5) SSH host key trust
====================================================================
- The deployment workflows deliberately do NOT set ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING=False
  or StrictHostKeyChecking=no.
- The self-hosted runner's known_hosts must already trust both
  cms1.operations.access-ci.org and the inventory-resolved endpoint for
  beta-operations.access-ci.org before the first real run, or every SSH/Ansible
  step will fail closed.
- If there is no existing trust relationship, add a "populate known_hosts"
  step (e.g. from an SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS secret populated via ssh-keyscan -H run
  from the bastion) rather than disabling verification.

====================================================================
Not required to change
====================================================================
- .github/CODEOWNERS is already correct for this purpose.
- No workflow file can configure environment reviewers, deployment tag rules,
  protected-tag rulesets, runner labels, runner SSH credentials, or known_hosts;
  an authorized repository administrator must apply and verify those settings.
